correctness.rationale: For D=diag(1,-1), the projection T↦(T-DTD)/2 preserves the data and is contractive for numerical radius by unitary invariance and convexity. On the off-diagonal slice w=(|p|+|q|)/2, as seen by maximizing the expectation over relative vector phase and equal coordinate moduli. Hence the scalar (p-q)/(2m) is Schur for cost m>0; Schwarz–Pick gives rho≥2m(a+b)/(4m²+ab). The quadratic is negative at m=max(a,b)/2 and opens upward, forcing the displayed larger root. At that root u=a/(2m) and v=-b/(2m) lie strictly in (-1,1). The frozen B sends the two normalized nodes to u and v, and the two linear identities involving u+1/u and v+1/v give the exact prescribed values. The boundary envelope H lies strictly between 0 and 1 since A>2 and C<-2. Thus |p|+|q|=2m on the circle and is at most 2m in the disk by subharmonicity; taking radial limits gives the uniform supremum m. The disk automorphism sending the original nodes to 0,rho transports the rational map back by composition.
residual_risks: Finite diagnostic checks neither establish the analytic theorem nor address novelty; the proof does not classify arbitrary matrix data.

evidence: Put the normalized nodes at 0,t and coordinate zeros at alpha_1=t, alpha_2=0, with both r_j=1. The earlier family gives p(z)=c_1(z-t)(1-tz)/(1-alpha_0 z)² and q(z)=c_2 z/(1-alpha_0 z)². Comparing the constant and linear coefficients in the prior normalization gives alpha_0=|c_1|t=u and |c_2|=(1-u/t)(1-ut). Hence v=q(t)=(t-u)/(1-ut). Conversely at t=(u+v)/(1+uv), the coefficients c_1=-u/t, c_2=(1-u/t)(1-ut)>0 are admissible and that source supplies a rational geodesic.

Substitution u=a/(2m), v=b/(2m) gives t=2m(a+b)/(4m²+ab); solving for the larger root gives exactly the frozen cost. The resulting off-diagonal map has that cost, so rational attainment is also covered.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This uses only contractive projection, endpoint evaluation and a quadratic rescaling of a known exact geodesic. No additional extremal principle or new asymmetric parameter estimate survives.

originality.rationale: The correct formula and rational attainment are mechanically covered by the earlier complex ellipsoid geodesic classification. The whole matrix interpolation problem for these data is exactly the off-diagonal ℓ1 slice by the contractive projection; there is no separate matrix feasibility obstruction. Jarnicki–Pflug–Zeinstra's theorem includes p1=p2=1/2, not just strictly convex Euclidean ellipsoids. The general geodesic formulas verified in Edigarian's m=1 specialization supply the exact cross-axis curve for unequal positive amplitudes, not only the balanced case.
residual_risks: The older paper is not claimed to use matrix language or to literally print M. The coverage is a demonstrated implication through an isometric slice and a contractive projection. Priority between the matching-date matrix records is not asserted.
